newsitem.title: USA: Spurned girlfriend torches homes on U.S. base.
newsitem.headline: Spurned girlfriend torches homes on U.S. base.

text.p: A fire allegedly set by an 18-year-old woman after a quarrel with her boyfriend raced through a townhouse complex at California's Travis Air Force Base, badly damaging six homes, officials said Thursday.
Police in the nearby town of Fairfield said they arrested Dawnesha Providence on suspicion of arson after Wednesday afternoon's blaze which displaced 17 people but caused no injuries.

They said Providence put a bundle of clothes in a bathtub and set them on fire after a dispute with her boyfriend, a military man who had recently moved into a townhouse at Travis Air Force Base, 50 miles northeast of San Francisco.

The fire quickly spread through the townhouse complex, totally destroying three of the six units in the building and causing extensive damage to the other three, base spokesman Sgt. Mark Kinkade said.
Air Force members and their families live in the two- and three-bedroom townhouses.

Fairfield police said the incident began when Providence's boyfriend refused to let her move in with him. The boyfriend, who was not named by police, left the house and told Providence he expected her to be gone when he came back.
"When he was gone, the girlfriend put a bundle of clothing in the bathtub and set the clothing on fire," a police statement said.
Providence left the house burning and went to find her boyfriend. They both returned to find the townhouse destroyed and several others engulfed in flames, police said.

About 60 firefighters from the base and nearby towns took about two hours to put out the blaze, Kinkade said. Police estimated structural damage at more than $250,000, not counting personal property losses.

Providence told base police officers at the scene that she had started the fire, police said. She was turned over to Fairfield police who booked her into Solano County Jail for investigation of five counts of arson, they said.

Kinkade said four families were living in the recently-renovated townhouse complex and two of the homes were unoccupied. Few people were home at the time, and those who were there could only save a few possessions, he said.
